slot.brief: A man in an accelerating lift with a weighing scale; ask for the scale reading given the lift's acceleration (pseudo-force framing).

stem: A man of mass $50$ kg stands on a weighing scale inside a lift accelerating upward at $2$ m s$^{-2}$. The reading of the scale (in kg wt) is (Take $g = 10$ m s$^{-2}$).

verdicts.working: Normal force = m(g+a) = 50(10+2) = 600 N. In kg wt, the reading is 600/10 = 60 kg wt.
issues: Options label the readings as kg rather than kg wt; the numerical answer is unchanged.

working:
Apparent weight $N = m(g+a) = 50 \times (10+2) = 600\ \text{N}$.
Scale reading in kg wt $= N/g = 600/10 = 60$ kg.

Independent check: Normal force = m(g+a) = 50(10+2) = 600 N. In kg wt, the reading is 600/10 = 60 kg wt.
solution:
For upward acceleration, the scale’s normal force is $N=m(g+a)$.
$$N=50(10+2)=600\,\text{N},\qquad \text{reading in kg wt}=\frac{N}{g}=\frac{600}{10}=60\,\text{kg wt}.$$
